$comment: Acceptance criteria from docs/remediation-plan.md, made executable. Each guardrail's `baseline` is the violation count measured on the audit date. CI fails when a count rises ABOVE its baseline, so debt can only shrink. When a fix lands, run `npm run evals -- --update-baselines` and commit the lowered number — that turns the guardrail into a permanent regression test.

guardrails.title: No golf metaphor in user-facing strings
guardrails.$note: 'scorecard' is deliberately NOT banned — a 1950s road-trip ledger can legitimately be a scorecard (maintainer call, 2026-08-15). The second half of this pattern was added after the first rewrite pass: the quiz modal shipped 'Pinseeker Challenge', 'Clubhouse Shot Tracker', 'Shot N of M' and 'Punch N', none of which the original pattern caught. A guardrail that misses a class gets widened, not excused.
guardrails.pattern: \bcaddie\b|\btee off\b|\bfairway\b|green in reg|\blayup\b|\bbirdie\b|on the bag|walk off the green|\bthe green\b|\bhole\b|1st tee|18th|\bpinseeker\b|\bclubhouse\b|shot tracker|flushed it|caught the rough|\bmulligan\b|\bputt\b|\bputter\b|putting green

guardrails.title: No claim of AI capability the app does not have
Docs may not name a dependency the project no longer has
Centroid distance may not be called travel
No hardcoded key material presented as encryption
guardrails.$note: legacy-save-reader.service.ts is excluded deliberately: it reproduces the <= 1.1.0 key constants for DECRYPT ONLY, so players upgrading do not lose their trip. It has no encrypt path. Delete the file and this exclusion once no supported upgrade starts below 1.2.0 (dec-0009).

guardrails.title: CSP may not allow unsafe-eval
Pinch zoom may never be disabled (WCAG 1.4.4)
Text colour may not use black at low alpha
A background token may not be used as a text colour
guardrails.note: Cream text on a fixed coloured fill was written as --app-bg-cream in four places. That token inverts to near-black in dark mode, so the label vanished into its own chip. Fixed fills take --app-ink-on-fill; only surfaces take --app-bg-*.

guardrails.title: An ephemera-only stylesheet may not use a themed ink token
guardrails.note: The quiz pass is printed matter end to end: every ground in the sheet is fixed card stock, so a token that inverts in dark mode has nothing legitimate to sit on (dec-0015). Three of these shipped invisible to a phone because scripts/contrast-audit.js only walks routes, never overlays (pm-0003). Include-list membership is the criterion: add any stylesheet here whose component draws only ephemera. The runtime twin of this check is the 'ink discipline' describe in quiz-modal.component.spec.ts, which catches the same class for tokens this pattern does not name.

guardrails.title: Safe-area insets go through the tokens, never raw env()
guardrails.note: Android's WebView leaves env(safe-area-inset-*) at its 0px fallback, so a component reaching for env() directly gets no inset and slides under the system navigation bar once edge-to-edge is enforced (targetSdk 35+). Capacitor's SystemBars plugin measures the real insets natively and injects --safe-area-inset-*; src/theme/variables.scss folds those into --app-safe-* with env() as the iOS/web fallback. Components use the --app-* tokens. variables.scss is excluded because it is where the fallback legitimately lives.

guardrails.title: currentColor is inert inside a background-image data URI
guardrails.note: An SVG used as an image is its own document, so currentColor there resolves to the initial black rather than inheriting the element colour. The four bottom-nav glyphs were black in both themes for this reason — invisible on the dark tags, and the active tab drew a rust label beside a black icon. Use mask-image + background-color: currentColor instead.

guardrails.title: No CLI analytics UUID committed
State flags stay small enough to render at 56px
guardrails.$note: Covers both extensions on purpose — flags are hybrid SVG/WebP since dec-0010, and an oversized raster must fail exactly like an oversized vector.

guardrails.title: The unused ionicons SVG directory is not copied into the build
Lazy routes are not all preloaded at boot
Release APK is shrunk by R8
No component method that nothing binds
Every animating stylesheet honours prefers-reduced-motion
The atlas SVG has no focusable children
Every injectable service has a spec file
package.json version matches android versionName
No example.com placeholders in anything published to a store
guardrails.note: All URLs and the contact address are real and live. The privacy policy is served at https://justsmitty.github.io/tagspotter_v3/privacy-policy.html, which is the URL in both store metadata files, so a placeholder reappearing here is publicly visible immediately.

guardrails.title: Release signing must not reference the debug keystore
guardrails.note: Every build so far was signed with the debug keystore for on-device smoke tests, done by invoking apksigner directly and never by committing it. This keeps it that way: a debug key committed into the release signing path would produce an APK that installs fine and can never be updated on Play.

guardrails.title: The iOS target stays iPhone-only
guardrails.$note: Capacitor scaffolds every iOS target as universal ("1,2"), and the project sat that way with no iPad layout, no iPad testing and no iPad screenshots — a universal binary obliges Apple to review it on iPad and obliges the listing to carry 13-inch screenshots. Portrait-only (con-0005) is the Android position and iPad was never the second half of a plan. Regenerating the Xcode project restores the default silently, which is exactly the kind of regression a baseline catches. See dec-0016.

guardrails.title: Info.plist requires arm64, the architecture the app actually ships
guardrails.$note: Capacitor scaffolds UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities as armv7, a 32-bit ISA. The deployment target is iOS 15, so the binary has no armv7 slice and no device that can install the app is 32-bit - the key declared a requirement the app cannot satisfy and that filters nothing. Same regression shape as ios-ipad-target: a value nobody chose, restored silently when the Xcode project is regenerated. The pattern is the element form rather than the bare token so the explanatory comment in Info.plist, which names armv7 deliberately, does not trip it - the defect has an exact shape and matching that shape is more precise than matching the word. See f-052.

guardrails.title: Screenshot-only hooks never enter the shipped index.html
guardrails.$note: The store-screenshot build injects two same-origin scripts into the BUILT web assets - screenshot-route.js (start route) and screenshot-seed.js (the window global PreferenceStorageService reads). Both exist so no seed or route override ships to players: in a real build the global is undefined and the branch in preference-storage.service.ts is dead. Committing either tag into src/index.html would ship a fake 28-state save and a forced start route to every player, and it would look exactly like a working app in review. The scan is on the source index.html only; www/ is build output and is where these belong. See f-053.

guardrails.title: Info.plist answers the export-compliance question up front
guardrails.$note: Without ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, App Store Connect asks the export-compliance question on every single build upload and the build sits in "Missing Compliance" until someone answers it by hand. The app ships no encryption of its own (dec-0009 — plain JSON saves), so the answer is false and never changes. Paired-pattern rather than regex-scan: this guardrail fires on ABSENCE, so the trigger is a key the file always has.

guardrails.title: Every sharedpref <exclude> in the backup rules names a file the app can produce
guardrails.$note: pm-0002. Both rule files excluded 'CapacitorStorage.temp_quiz_session.xml' for two releases; no such file has ever existed, because temp_quiz_session is a KEY inside Capacitor Preferences and domain="sharedpref" selects files. Android does not warn on an exclude that matches nothing, so the build stayed green while every reader believed the sidecar was held back. The producible set is DERIVED from the Preferences group (default CapacitorStorage, plus any Preferences.configure group in src), not listed here — a real second group makes a matching exclude legal on its own, and an invented filename stays a violation. This guardrail cannot tell you the exclusion is the RIGHT one, only that it is not inert; the resume-path guard in HomeWorkflowService is what actually holds the invariant.
